_about: Reconciliation ledger for the schema census gate (conformance/selfcheck/verify_schema_census.py, PLAN-0825 A.3 / G0-c). Every schema/service file in the pinned vendored corpus must be either REFERENCED by a register row (a future schema_enforced:true row whose `source` points into source/schemas/ or source/services/ -- none exist at any pinned version yet, so today's honest referenced count is 0, not a bug) or RULED here. A ruling is a recorded, spec-grounded, hash-pinned acknowledgement that a specific file needs no row of its own (e.g. a deliberately out-of-scope vertical, or a non-normative $defs-only helper fragment already covered by its parent schema's own row). Each ruling's `hash` is the file's SHA-256 content hash AT RULING TIME; if the live vendored hash no longer matches (a re-pin changed the file), the ruling goes STALE and the file reverts to effectively un-ruled until a human re-reviews the new content and updates the hash (P-2 fail-noisy self-expiry -- a ruling can never quietly keep covering changed content). This tool is REPORT-ONLY by default (see verify_schema_census.py's own doctrine); pass --enforce to gate on unreferenced/stale findings, which stays a later, deliberate flip. Empty today -- no schema file has been ruled yet at any pinned version.
